what: WORKED COMPUTATION (independent run 1 of 2): SETTING (the owner's working reading, 2026-09-20; block 39, the open PR titled 'ail39: records that move'): a site is empty or carries ONE record; a record carries its content (six axes); two neighbouring records weigh W = c * omega, omega = p, q, r for equal, opposite, orthogonal axes; a bond with an empty end weighs 1; the axioms' rule K (normalized over contents) does not depend on the scale c. MOTION: a record chooses between its position and an empty neighbouring position in proportion to the pair weights it would have there; this is in detailed balance with the static law on the occupied set. The neutral scale c_0 = 6/(p + q + 4r): an empty neighbour weighs what a record of random content weighs on average, and it is the least scale at which the law with vacancies is reflection positive through bond planes. Simulator: probes/lib/moving_gas.py p q r scale rho L sweeps seed (scale = a number or the word neutral). A first theory of the clumping onset. For the six-axis gas with vacancies (weights c * (p, q, r); empty bonds 1) write the mean-field free energy per site as a function of the density rho and the content distribution (six occupation fractions), find where the uniform disordered state loses stability to (i) a density modulation and (ii) alignment, and where a dense aligned phase coexists with a dilute one. Give the onset p*(c, rho) on the line (p,1,2) at c = neutral, 1, 1/2 and rho = 0.3 and compare with the executed brackets (neutral: 8-12, near 10; scale 1: 5-6; scale 1/2: 8-12) and with the logs under logs/probes/X:moving-clumping-line-p12/ when present. Expectation: mean field puts the onset too low by tens of percent, with the right ordering in c. DELIVERABLE in your unit worktree: probes/work/compute/moving-meanfield-onset/<your worker name>/run.py (self-contained; exact arithmetic wherever the statement is exact; numpy only for the numerical cross-checks named) and RESULT.md (the table or formulas, in plain text). run.py prints one line per result, a final `SUMMARY: <the main result in one line>`, and `HIT: <what>` ONLY if a result contradicts the expectation stated in the task (that is the interesting case: report it precisely). Two workers do each computation independently; the supervisor compares them. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/compute/moving-meanfield-onset/<name>/run.py"
